title: Advice for improvement?
author: SocialContractGuy
selftext:
Hey everyone!  
I’ve been working on a browser-based strategy/simulation game called **The Social Contract**, and I’d love to get some feedback from people who have experience with AI-assisted game development.

**https://thesocialcontractgame.com**

The idea is that you build and govern your own island nation. You make decisions about laws, public services, infrastructure, education, healthcare, defense, and more. Your choices affect your citizens’ happiness, the economy, and the overall success of your government.  
There’s also a free-roam mode where you can explore your island, along with random events, political decisions, and other challenges.  
I’m an 8th-grade Civics teacher, and this originally started as a project for my students to explore government and political philosophy in a more interactive way. It’s gradually turned into something much bigger, and I’m hoping to eventually develop it into a more polished standalone game.

I’ve been using AI to help with development, and while I’ve made a lot of progress, there are definitely areas that still need work, particularly the visuals, gameplay depth, and overall user experience.

**I’d really appreciate some honest feedback:**  
What’s your first impression of the game?  
What feels unfinished or needs the most improvement?

Are the gameplay mechanics interesting enough to keep someone playing?  
What would you prioritize improving next?  
Feel free to be critical. I’m still learning, and I’d much rather hear what isn’t working than just get compliments.  
Thanks to anyone who takes the time to check it out!

comments.author: SocialContractGuy
comments.body: Anyone want to try it out?
